description:
The /fly HUD speed readout shows 'NaN km/s' for outer-planet missions (Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune, Pluto, Ceres — 20 missions in the catalog) once the spacecraft's heliocentric distance exceeds ~2.5 AU. Moon and Mars missions are unaffected.

Expected: The HUD speed always shows a finite number (in km/s) for every spacecraft position along any mission's trajectory. No NaN ever appears in the speed readout. Mars missions retain the current ~32.7 km/s departure reading at r≈1 AU.

Acceptance criteria:
- The HUD heliocentricKms value must be finite (not NaN, not Infinity) for every scR value reachable along any mission's outbound arc — including Jupiter (r=5.2 AU), Saturn (r=9.5 AU), Neptune (r=30 AU), Pluto (r=39.5 AU) [code-invariant: NaN in production — the app must not display NaN as a user-facing value]
- The Earth-departure speed for Mars-bound missions (activeDestination='mars') must remain ~32.7 km/s at r≈1 AU (the current Earth-Mars Hohmann value, unchanged) [reporter: "keep the inputs as they are; the speed function's out-of-range behavior is the bug" — the reporter confirmed the Earth-Mars Hohmann SMA is correct for Mars departures]

Domain facts:
- The destination's semi-major axis is available at runtime via DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a (imported at +page.svelte:65 from $lib/lambert-grid.constants)
- outboundArc at mission-arc.ts:93 already computes a = (R_EARTH_AU + destA) / 2 per destination — the HUD call site at line 952 is the only place that doesn't
- The cislunar view already computes speed via finite-difference at +page.svelte:5642-5645 (speedKms = Math.hypot(vx, vy, vz)) as an alternative pattern in the same file

Target: src/routes/fly/+page.svelte — heliocentricKms $derived at lines 951-953
Do NOT change src/lib/orbital/fly-physics.ts :: heliocentricSpeed — the vis-viva implementation whose radicand goes negative when fed a hardcoded Mars SMA; the failed patch added a sqrt(µ/r) fallback here, treating the symptom (NaN output) rather than the cause (wrong SMA at the call site) — it is not the owner of this symptom.
